name: CA-26
label: Likely D

key_factors: District's D+9 partisan lean favors the Democratic nominee
Jacqui Irwin has a large money advantage in both candidate and outside spending
Open seat removes incumbent advantage and adds some uncertainty
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%
model.rationale: The seat's D+9 lean and Irwin's clear fundraising edge point to a Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 96%. The open-seat nature and absence of any polling warrant a modest haircut from the fundamentals-based margin, but not enough to move it out of Likely D.
model.watch: If Gallucci consolidates Republican support and attracts outside money while Irwin's cash advantage erodes, the race could tighten toward Lean D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Julia Brownley's retirement leaves this Ventura County-area seat open, but the district's D+9 partisan lean keeps it favorable ground for Democrats. State assemblymember Jacqui Irwin enters as the Democratic nominee with a substantial financial edge, having raised more than double her Republican rival Sam Gallucci and holding a large cash-on-hand advantage, plus outside groups are spending on her behalf with none opposing.

Gallucci has struggled to raise money and has little cash remaining, limiting his ability to introduce himself to voters. With no public polling in the race, the forecast leans on the district's fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democratic side near 96%. The open-seat dynamic is the main source of uncertainty, but the evidence points to a Democratic hold.
